x: A little further back came Tobin in 12th position, followed by Lucas 19th, Morrell 22nd, and Murdoch 36th. Our next man was round about the 50 mark.
Patience (4th) and he appeared to be running very strongly. Then they came thick and fast, but to my surprise Tobin was our second man in the 7th position.

A further invitation having been given by the Union Sportive Metropolitaine for us to compete in the above event was accepted and the following team was chosen to represent the Club: Carter, Cohen, Footer, Patience D., Parker, Penny, Tobin and Verney, accompanied by W.
Arthur Penny had come through in great style but still had a good leeway to make up on the leaders. Dick Tobin was in front with A.

Tobin had caught Frank Webb and they were having a regular argument, because Tobin could run uphill and no one can catch Frank going down, and the course was full of short, sharp ups and downs with a real pull here and there.

The sixth of the original fast pack, Jerman, was back another 50 yards with Tobin, Arthur Allum, and Murdock, on his heels. Others to finish were Tobin (20), E.
Has any member any news of their whereabouts? Tobin; who when last seen in the street complained he had heard nothing from the Club.
However " there's many a slip twix cup and lip." Mitcham won the first leg, with Tobin taking 3rd place. The next lap went to Epsom, with Bert Mitchell 3rd.

Our first man home was Dick Tobin who had been troubled by cramp in the Upminster race and then followed Bert Smith and Syd Ring who came in together.

The others followed at short intervals, Charlton 20th, Tobin 38th, Heard and Ken Stimpson 50th, MacDonald 60th and Housego 130th. The next time we saw them, which was about 5 miles, Ferguson had opened up a gap between Field and Thompson; our runners were round about the same as before.
Positions of our men were—4, Tobin; 5, McDonald; 8, Stimpson; 10, Whitehead; 14, Penstone. In the Mitcham A.C. 15 miles open road race we had quite a good number of our members competing and B.

Going back that far reminds me of that exceptional performance in 1945 when with Burfitt (1), Main (2), Pearson (3) and Eeles (13) Belgrave 'A' won with 19 points, to be followed by Tobin (5), Clinton (7), Smart (17) and Jarlett (26) who brought home Belgrave 'B' in second place.

1938 was a quiet year for Ted but in the first few days of January 1939 he finished second in the Middlesex Cross-country championship, and the Cadogan A.C. team (consisting entirely of Belgrave runners as follows:- Stimpson 2, D. Patience 4, Shields 7, Allum 14, Tobin 15, F.R.
Tobin of Swansea was the winner in 30:14 with Brighton & Hove's P.Bristow 2nd, just 5 seconds ahead of our man. With Stu' Paton 8th in 31:11 and Jon Hobbs 12th in 31:45 the Bels took 4th team place.
